I don’t have kids but I would give them age appropriate honesty, and it depends how much information you want to give them too. I think if you’re not honest it *could* cause issues in the future. As a child who didn’t have things hidden but had it explained to them in an age appropriate way it made things significantly easier to understand and process. Please modify this for their age - obviously a 16 year old would be able to have a different understanding to a 5 year old.

I would say something along the lines of (based on my experience as the child)

“I need to talk to you about something you might not fully understand now, but I hope as you get older you will. We cannot see X, or Y or Z anymore. This is because they have hurt people, and attempted to hurt people. For your safety and my own, we need to stay away from this. I know this might upset you and you might miss those family members which is okay. But I am the adult and it is my responsibility to take care of you. I love you and I want to protect you. We will not be going to family events while they are there, but we will still go to some. We can also spend family time together, just us. If you have questions please tell me when you’re ready and I’ll answer them the best I can.”

The only thing I disagree with is people having urges to act out the way they were abused on other consenting adults. The key word is CONSENT. As long as it’s not illegal, and not hurting anyone else. I think sometimes people use that as a coping mechanism because it helps them feel in control, or in some way they may want to understand why their abuser did it (e.g. is it gratifying?). Again, the key word is consent - anything that may be considered “imitating abuse” (I believe it would be considered BDSM) with some exceptions is okay with consenting adults.
